title: Safehouse and Cipher
premise: Rafael Marchetti, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call that ended in a body bag, has spent years hiding a second life: they were trained as a cipher-keeper by a covert network that brokers leverage over governments. When a realtor's listing exposes the safe house — interiors photographed down to Rafael's coded notebooks — the network's hunters converge, and Rafael realizes the listing was bait set by someone who knows their tradecraft intimately. Forced to ally with the estranged trainees who once shared that house, Rafael must decrypt the network's ledger and burn it from within. In the end, Rafael trades themself to the network's founder to buy the others time, walks out of the final negotiation having turned the founder's own people, and chooses the fragile found family over the polished lie.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to strangers talk themselves back from ledges before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town she refuses to name, where she keeps her own go-bag out of habit.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Mid-negotiation with a barricaded father, Rafael gets an alert: the old safe house is on the market, photos showing the chalkboard cipher wall they thought was painted over. The emotional beat is cold recognition — someone wanted this found. Rafael closes the negotiation flawlessly while privately unraveling, then drives past the house at night and sees a light on inside.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with a flashback to training under a mentor called only Wren. We learn the network, Meridian, trains 'keepers' to memorize and destroy its ledger of compromised officials. Rafael packed a go-bag for eight years waiting for this day. The beat is dread braided with longing: the house was the only place Rafael belonged. A tail confirms the photos weren't accidental.

chapters.title: Three Keys
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Rafael and former trainee Odile Vasseur, now a forensic accountant, who received the same listing. They meet at a diner neither trusts, trading accusations about who leaked. The beat is friction masking grief — they haven't spoken since the failed negotiation that killed fellow trainee Sam. They agree to a temporary truce: find who listed the house before Meridian finds them.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Posing as buyers, Rafael and Odile tour the safe house during its open house and find signs someone has been living there: fresh coffee, a child's drawing of the chalkboard. Hidden in the attic, a message in Wren's cipher: 'The ledger is awake. Come home or be inventory.' The beat shifts from investigation to summons — the trap has a door left deliberately open.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Meridian makes contact through Odile's bank accounts, freezing then unfreezing them as a demonstration. A handler named Corliss offers absolution in exchange for the third trainee, Marcus Reyes, who stole a fragment of the ledger. Odile hides the offer from Rafael. The beat is corruption as seduction — Meridian doesn't threaten family; it offers to become one.

chapters.title: What Sam Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Digging into Sam's death, Rafael discovers it wasn't a negotiation failure but a Meridian test Rafael unknowingly passed by keeping silent. Guilt inverts: Rafael didn't fail Sam; the network used Rafael's loyalty as a weapon. The beat is rage crystallizing into purpose. Rafael tells Odile the truth, and the truce becomes a vow.

chapters.title: The Fragment
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Hiding in Lisbon, Marcus decodes his ledger fragment and finds Wren's name among the compromised — the mentor sold them all years ago. Meridian's cleaners close in; Marcus calls the only number he still trusts. The beat is betrayal at the story's root, reframing every memory of the safe house as curated. He agrees to meet Rafael in Marseille.

chapters.title: Marseille Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The reunion is ambushed — Corliss anticipated it, and Wren appears, alive and working both sides. Rafael negotiates live, using hostage techniques on the people who trained them, buying Marcus's exit by surrendering a decoy cipher key. The beat is Rafael's craft turned inward: every technique Meridian taught, used to unmake Meridian. Wren slips Rafael a location: the archive vault.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. Inside the vault, the trio splits the ledger decryption across three minds so no one person can be leveraged. Corliss takes Rafael hostage — the negotiator finally on the wrong side of the table. Rafael talks Corliss's own team into standing down, exposing that Corliss falsified records to climb. The beat is power devouring itself while the found family holds the line.

chapters.title: Sold, As Is
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, resolution. The ledger goes public in fragments; Meridian dissolves into infighting. Wren, exposed and diminished, offers Rafael succession — the corrupted inheritance refused. The trio buys the safe house together at auction, cheap because of its notoriety, and paints the cipher wall white. Final beat: Rafael unpacks the go-bag at last, keeping only the notebook, blank now, first page of something honest.
